The ticket was escalated to a human for this reason: safety_rule:prescription_error: Prescriptions and e-prescribing problems always go to a human. (also matched: suspected_outage) Acknowledge the customer's problem and say a member of the support team is handling it. Do not promise an outcome or a timeline. Give product steps only if a knowledge-base article is provided and it answers the ticket, and take them only from that article. Put the reply in draft.

Reply with only a JSON object and no other text.
Output: review_draft.
The JSON object must match this JSON schema:
{"additionalProperties": false, "description": "A suggested reply for the human agent who takes an escalation.", "properties": {"draft": {"minLength": 1, "title": "Draft", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["draft"], "title": "review_draft", "type": "object"}

Article: none

Ticket:
Assistance Required for Updating Pharmacy Out-of-Stock Notification Preferences

Dear Support Team,

I am writing to request guidance on managing medication substitution workflows and out-of-stock alerts within our patient management system. Earlier today, one of our physicians attempted to switch an unavailable prescription to an alternative agent, but the notification flags did not route properly to the designated pharmacy.

We have checked the provider settings and ensured that our local pharmacy directory is up to date, but the substitution messaging tabs appear greyed out on certain patient profiles. Could you please provide instructions on how our front desk and clinical staff can correctly configure these alert pathways so future notifications transmit without error?

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Sincerely,
Front Office Coordinator

I’ve escalated this to a member of our support team who will investigate the problem further. They will be in touch with you shortly to gather any additional details needed and to work toward a resolution.

We appreciate your patience while we look into this.

Best regards,
[Support Team]"
